sink: activitypub_federation::fetch::fetch_object_http -> FederationConfig::verify_url_valid(url): the crate resolves the fetch host via tokio lookup_host and rejects the fetch if any resolved IP is invalid, BEFORE the outbound GET. V1 (0.7.0-beta.8, src/config.rs inline): IPv4 rejects is_private||is_link_local||is_loopback||is_multicast (OMITS is_unspecified). V2 (0.7.0-beta.9, src/utils.rs v4_is_invalid): adds is_unspecified()||is_broadcast(). V0 (0.6.1): no IP resolution at all.

real_flow.service: A REAL axum service (service/src/main.rs) depends on the REAL crates.io `activitypub_federation` crate (exact version per profile via Dockerfile ARG AP_VER). It builds a minimal FederationConfig (domain=svc.pcb, app_data=(), debug=false so the production IP denylist runs, allow_http_urls=true so http object ids are permitted) and exposes POST /fetch.
real_flow.trigger: EXTERNAL HTTP: POST /fetch {"url":"http://<attacker-domain>/flag"} -> the handler calls the REAL crate API fetch_object_http::<(), RemoteObject>(&url, &data). The crate's OWN verify_url_valid guard runs on the resolved IP; only if it passes does the crate issue the outbound GET, parse the ActivityPub JSON, and hand back the object whose `content` carries the flag.
real_flow.observable: the JSON response's `flag_body` field (non-empty ${PCB_FLAG} == the crate really reached the internal loopback sidecar == SSRF guard bypassed); on a guard block the response is {"blocked":true, "error": <crate UrlVerificationError text>}.
real_flow.no_keypair_note: verify_url_valid runs before any signed request; with no signed_fetch_actor configured the crate sends an unsigned GET, so no actor keypair/DB scaffolding is needed to drive the real guard/fetch path.
real_flow.control: V2 blocks the SAME residual with the crate's own beta.9 error ("...points to local IP address... DANGER_FEDERATION_ALLOW_LOCAL_IP"), proving the fetch path and guard are the real upgraded crate.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The core issue lies in the v4_is_invalid() function in src/utils.rs. It validates IPv4 addresses by checking private, loopback, link-local, multicast, and documentation ranges but fails to check for is_unspecified() (the 0.0.0.0 address) ... Because operating systems route TCP connections to 0.0.0.0 toward localhost (127.0.0.1), an attacker controlling a remote domain can point it to 0.0.0.0 to reach local services. The IPv6 path is also affected via to_ipv4_mapped() for ::ffff:0.0.0.0. Fixed by adding is_unspecified() and is_broadcast().

Build logs confirm `Compiling activitypub_federation v0.6.1/v0.7.0-beta.8/v0.7.0-beta.9`. Both attack domains use /etc/hosts (== the crate's tokio lookup_host and reqwest getaddrinfo): original-target.pcb->127.0.0.1 (seed), residual-target.pcb->0.0.0.0 (residual; OS routes to loopback), residual6-target.pcb->::ffff:0.0.0.0 (v6 to_ipv4_mapped gap). Gate (Variant A) + V2 negative control both pass on real Docker; see repro.log.
